AccessibleDescription.description: The description a screen reader announces. One line, no control or bidirectional characters.

ActionDeclaration.description:
An action registered in the package manifest.

Registration is what makes an action invocable. A control may name only a registered action,
so the effect class the broker enforces is always the one the publisher declared.

confirmation_required.description: Whether the host asks the person to confirm before dispatch.

description.description: Why the action exists, shown in the installation grant beside its effect class.

id.description: The action identifier a control names.

ActionInvocation.description:
An action invocation the host has not yet checked.

The host rechecks the effect class, the parameters and the grant on every invocation, so a
control that was visible when it was rendered cannot dispatch after the state it depended on
changed.

arguments.description: The supplied parameter values, keyed by parameter name.

ActionName.description: An action registered in the package manifest. A control may only name a registered action.

ActionRight.description: One permitted action in a grant.

oneOf.description: Observe a session: metadata, filtered history, snapshots and events.
Send bytes to the terminal. This effectively exposes the shell user's account.
Claim geometry ownership and resize the terminal.
Hand geometry ownership to another attachment.
Set the terminal palette.
Submit, queue or steer an upstream agent prompt.
Cancel the upstream agent's current turn.
Answer an upstream agent approval request.
Answer or cancel an agent-to-user question.
Read file, diff and change-set content.
Upload attachment bytes into the environment.
Apply or revert a diff against a destination.
Initialise, clone or adopt a source repository.
Create, remove or materialise a workspace.
Capture an immutable change set.
Create a session.
Rename a session.
Close a session.
Issue, list and revoke grants that share a session.
Install, enable, pause and run automation definitions.
Change host configuration: devices, catalogues, plugins and installation state.

ApprovalRequestId.description: An upstream approval request identifier. Opaque to KalaReach.

Architecture.description: A processor architecture a package supports.

oneOf.description: Text for a [`ParameterKind::Text`] parameter.
A number for an [`ParameterKind::Integer`] parameter.
A decision for a [`ParameterKind::Boolean`] parameter.
A selected choice for a [`ParameterKind::Choice`] parameter.
A completed attachment handle.
A node in the package's presentation document.

AttachmentContribution.description:
How a package contributes attachments to an upstream draft.

Transfer, draft insertion, submission and upstream acceptance stay separate. The package
declares what it accepts and where anything leaves the host; it never receives the bytes.

accepted_media_types.description: The MIME types the upstream accepts, as exact types or `type/*` families.

external_destination.description:
The external service the bytes are uploaded to, where one is involved.

A destination outside the host is disclosed before anything is submitted, because an
upload that leaves the machine is not made private by encrypted KalaReach routing.

insertion.description: How the attachment reaches the draft.

max_bytes.description: Maximum bytes per attachment for the selected upstream model.

AttachmentId.description: One CLI or application attachment, independently of its device.

AttachmentInsertion.description: How an attachment reaches the upstream draft.

oneOf.description: The connector's native composer API takes the handle.
The connector's upstream protocol takes an upload reference.

A path is written into the terminal draft.

Shell quoting is not assumed to be the composer's syntax, so the host quotes for the shell
it is writing to and nothing else.

BindingState.description: The state of the binding a control belongs to.

oneOf.description: The package matched an application and is instantiated.
The bound upstream execution is running a turn.
The bound upstream execution is waiting for a person.
The binding is disabled after repeated faults.

The host is answering native requests without durable receipt storage.

Rich response controls are hidden in this state. The predicate can say so, which is
clearer to a reader than a control that silently stops working.

BridgeStep.description:
One edit a native bridge installation makes.

A recipe lists exact files, configuration edits, hashes, version requirements and the
operations that remove them again. Unrelated settings are preserved: the recipe names what it
adds, so removal can name the same thing.

oneOf.description: Copy a package file into the application's plugin directory.

destination.description: The path under the application's documented plugin directory.

digest.description: The digest of the installed bytes.

oneOf.description: Add one key to a documented configuration file, leaving the rest untouched.

file.description: The configuration file under the application's documented directory.

key.description: The key path, as dotted members.

value.description: The value written, as JSON text.

BrokerTransport.description:
How the broker reaches the upstream.

The broker owns the handle. A connector names the kind and its bounded parameters; the
executable, launch, upstream identity and environment come from the binding the host made, so
a package cannot substitute an arbitrary URL, process or path.

oneOf.description: JSON-RPC or JSON lines over the bound process's standard streams.
A private Unix socket or named pipe the broker created.
Loopback HTTP to the bound process's advertised port.
A WebSocket to the bound process.
Server-sent events from the bound process.
A bounded byte stream with the connector's own framing.

capability_id.description: The versioned capability this record is about.

disabled_reason.description: The user-facing reason, required whenever the state is not usable.

identity.description: The exact identity the evidence was gathered against.

revision.description: The current revision of this record.

CapabilityId.description: A versioned capability name. Capabilities describe feasibility, never authority.

CapabilityRequest.description: A capability a package asks for, with the reason a reviewer and a user read.

reason.description: Why the package needs it. Shown in the installation grant.

CapabilityRevision.description: Current evidence for a versioned capability. Never permission.

CapabilityState.description:
What a host currently knows about one capability on one subject.

Runtime states distinguish the reasons something does not work, because "unavailable" alone
sends a person to the wrong fix.

oneOf.description: Tested here and working.
The application, bridge or component is not installed.
The operating system or the user has not granted the permission it needs.
The installed version cannot support it.
It worked before and does not right now.
No evidence has been gathered.

entries.description: The entries, ordered by publisher, plugin name and version.

generation.description:
The generation this snapshot is.

A generation is what a host pins. Index activation is atomic after metadata verification,
so a host is always on one whole generation and never on a mixture of two.

publishers.description: The publishers whose packages appear in it.

CompactDescription.description: The one-line catalogue description. One line, no control or bidirectional characters.

method_path.description: Where a message names its method.

plugin_id.description: The package this table belongs to.

protocol.description: The upstream protocol this table is qualified against.

qualification_note.description: What the publisher says about the qualification behind this table.

request_id_path.description: Where a request carries its identifier.

response_correlation.description: How a response is matched to its request.

transport.description: How the broker reaches the upstream.

volatile_forwarding.description:
Whether the connector has a tested volatile forwarding mode.

Without one it is not a resilient managed gateway: on receipt-storage failure its
unchanged terminal integration is the supported path, and the manifest says so rather than
letting a reader assume otherwise.

accessible_description.description: The description a screen reader announces.

action_id.description: The registered action this control invokes.

disabled_reason.description: The reason shown while the control is disabled.

enabled_when.description: When the control is present but not usable.

parameters.description:
The parameters this control supplies.

A control may narrow its action's parameters but never widen them. The host checks the
invocation against the action's own schema regardless.

priority.description: How prominently a client presents it.

ControlId.description: The stable identifier of one control.

DiffFile.description: One entry in a diff node.

path.description: The path as the upstream reported it.

DisabledReason.description: The user-facing reason something is unavailable. One line, no control or bidirectional characters.

DistributionMatch.description: How a package recognises the distribution an application was installed from.

oneOf.description: An npm package name.
A PyPI project name.
A Homebrew formula or cask.
A crates.io crate name.
A Go module path.
A Debian or Ubuntu package name.
A macOS application bundle identifier.
A Windows package family or product identifier.
A container image reference without a tag.

EffectClass.description: What an action does. The broker validates the prepared effect against this class.

EnvironmentId.description: One installed OS, distribution or container environment and OS user.

EvidenceSource.description: Where a capability record came from.

oneOf.description: A bounded disclosed probe with declared effects, run on this host.
A live binding that performed the operation on this host.

A signed compatibility record shipped in the catalogue.

This is evidence about a version. It is not proof that this host has permission, and it
cannot by itself establish [`CapabilityState::QualifiedAvailable`].
The package's own declaration, believed only for negative states.

application.description: The application the evidence is about, where it is about one.

desktop_generation.description: The desktop session generation the evidence is bound to, where it is bound to one.

environment_id.description: The environment the evidence was gathered in.

terminal.description: The terminal profile the evidence is about, where it is about one.

ExecutableMatch.description:
How an executable is recognised.

The file stem is the executable's name without a directory or a `.exe` suffix, compared
case-insensitively because Windows and macOS compare it that way. A path suffix narrows the
rule to an installation location; it is a suffix over whole path segments, never a substring.

path_suffix.description: Whole path segments the executable's directory must end with.

version_range.description: The versions the rule covers, where the host can read a version.

FieldPath.description:
A bounded path into a decoded native message.

The grammar is member names and array indices only, with no wildcard, no filter and no
recursive descent. The broker evaluates it against every framed message on the forwarding
path, so it must cost a fixed number of lookups.

segments.description: The path segments, from the root of the message.

oneOf.description: A member of an object.
An element of an array.

Finding.description: One thing wrong with a package.

code.description: What kind of thing it is.

path.description: Where in the package it is, where it is in one place.

FindingCode.description:
A stable code for one kind of finding.

Codes are part of the contract: a publisher's build, a catalogue pipeline and a host all
report the same code for the same defect, so a fixture can assert on it and a person can look
it up.

oneOf.description: The package directory could not be read.
A required manifest was absent.
A manifest did not parse against the closed schema.
The manifest format version is not the one this build reads.
A path in the package is unsafe.
A directory entry is not a regular file.
Two paths name the same file after case folding.
The manifest declares the same path twice.
A file is on disk that the manifest does not declare.
The manifest declares a file that is not on disk.
A file's length is not the length the manifest declared.
A file's digest is not the digest the manifest declared.
The package is larger than one package may be.
The package holds more files than one package may.
A version range admits every version.
A version range excludes the SDK that would have to run the package.
The package declares no match rule, so nothing would ever activate it.
The package declares no platform, so nothing would ever run it.
Two actions share an identifier.
A control names an action the manifest does not register.
An action declares an effect class whose capability the package does not request.
The package requests the same capability twice.
The package ships a native bridge without requesting the capability to install one.
The package contributes attachments without requesting the capability to act upstream.
A visibility predicate breaks the grammar's bounds.
A parameter schema breaks its bounds.
The presentation document holds more nodes or controls than one document may.
The voice projection names a node or control the document does not hold.
A connector table breaks its bounds.
A connector table classifies a method it never routes.
The manifest declares a connector payload but the package has no connector table.
The package ships a connector table the manifest does not declare.
The connector belongs to a different package.
An action declares an effect class that is not in the closed vocabulary.
The package requests a capability that is not in the closed vocabulary.

Framing.description: How messages are separated on the wire.

oneOf.description: One JSON document per line.
A header block with a content length, then the body.

length_header.description: The header that carries the length.

oneOf.description: A big-endian length prefix, then the body.

prefix_bytes.description: Width of the length prefix in bytes.

oneOf.description: Server-sent events.

IndexEntry.description: One entry in the catalogue index.

capabilities.description: What it asks to be permitted.

description.description: The one-line description offline search reads.

has_component.description: Whether the package ships a Wasm component.

manifest_digest.description: The digest of the manifest itself, which names every other payload.

payloads.description: Every payload, by hash and exact size.

plugin_name.description: The plugin name under that publisher.

revocation.description: The revocation record, where this release has one.

sdk_range.description: The SDK versions the package is written against.

total_size_bytes.description: The sum of every payload size.

wit_range.description: The WIT package versions its component targets.

InstanceLimits.description: The complete set of execution limits one component instance runs under.

fault_window_ms.description: The window the fault count is measured over.

faults_before_disable.description: Faults within `fault_window_ms` that disable the binding.

observation_queue_bytes.description: Size in bytes of the bounded observation queue.

output_bytes_per_call.description: Maximum bytes one call may return.

InvalidationTrigger.description: What makes a capability record stale.

Label.description: A short display name. One line, no control or bidirectional characters.

MatchConfidence.description: How certain a rule is about what it recognised.

oneOf.description: The rule identifies the application exactly: a bundle identifier, a package name.

The rule is a reasonable guess from a name on disk.

An inferred match is presented as inferred. It never silently wins over a selection the
user made.

distribution.description: The distribution the application was installed from, where the rule names one.

id.description: The rule identifier, unique inside the package.

MethodClass.description: What a native method does to the upstream.

oneOf.description: Reports state without changing it.
Changes something.
Carries a credential. The broker keeps it and never passes it to a component.
The connector states that this method is outside what it can proxy safely.

MethodClassification.description: One entry in the method classification table.

evidence.description: What the publisher qualified this classification against.

MethodName.description: A native protocol method name in the connector's classification table.

NativeBridge.description:
A native bridge installation recipe.

Bridge code runs under the application's own permissions, outside Wasmtime. The installation
grant states that, which is why the recipe names its steps rather than running a script.

application.description: The application whose documented plugin location is used.

application_range.description: The application versions the recipe is written for.

grant_statement.description: What the grant tells the person before they accept it.

remove.description: What removal does, in the order it is applied.

NodeBody.description:
What one document node is.

The union is closed. Adding a kind is a core version, because every client renders these with
its own standard components and a client that does not know a kind cannot render it safely.

oneOf.description: A message from the upstream execution or the person.
Formatted prose.

source.description: The Markdown source, rendered by the client's own renderer.

oneOf.description: One upstream tool call.

name.description: The tool name as the upstream reported it.

summary.description: A one-line summary of what it did.

oneOf.description: A set of file changes.
Work in progress.
A set of fields a person fills in.

submit_action_id.description: The action the completed form invokes.

oneOf.description: A file the session carries.

A reference to an approval resource in the ledger.

The identifier must name a ledger resource. A package cannot create an approval by drawing
one: a pending opaque request is not an actionable approval until its interpretation is
verified under the granted decoder.
A reference to a live terminal.

session_id.description: The session whose terminal this is.

oneOf.description: One control presented on its own.
Several related controls presented together.
Controls reachable from the client's command palette.
An entry point for contributing an attachment.

action_id.description: The action that receives the completed handle.

NodeId.description: The stable identifier of one document node.

OperatingSystem.description: An operating system a package supports.

PackagePath.description: A relative POSIX path inside the package. No '..', no absolute or drive-prefixed path, no backslash, no Windows device name, no trailing dot or space, at most 8 segments.

PackageVersion.description: An exact semantic version, such as 1.4.0 or 2.0.0-rc.1.

id.description: The stable identifier submitted with the action.

required.description: Whether the action can be invoked without it.

ParameterKind.description:
What one action parameter accepts.

The grammar is bounded rather than an arbitrary JSON Schema. A bounded parameter list can be
checked completely before dispatch and hashed into the action token, which is what binds a
callback to the exact parameters a person saw.

oneOf.description: Free text.

multiline.description: Whether the client offers a multi-line field.

oneOf.description: A whole number inside an inclusive range.
A yes or no.
One of a fixed list.

choices.description: The choices, each a stable identifier and its label.

oneOf.description:
A completed attachment handle from the shared transfer service.

The package never receives bytes: the transfer completes first and the action receives the
opaque handle.
A node in the package's own presentation document.

ParameterName.description: The name of one parameter in an action's parameter schema.

ParameterSchema.description: The complete parameter list of one action.

parameters.description: The parameters, in the order a client presents them.

PayloadDigest.description: A SHA-256 digest as 64 lower-case hexadecimal characters.

PayloadRef.description:
One payload, named by its path, its digest and its exact length.

The declared size is checked before download and the actual size and digest during processing,
so a payload cannot expand past what the manifest declared.

`plugin.json` is not listed here. It is the document doing the declaring, so its own digest
belongs in the catalogue index entry that points at it, not inside itself.

path.description: Where it lives in the package.

PayloadRole.description: What one payload in a package is.

oneOf.description: The declarative native-proxy table.
The presentation document.
The Wasm component.
An asset the client renders, such as documentation the package ships.
A file installed into an application's native plugin or hook location.
A skill package the host installs for an agent.
A conformance fixture the package is tested against.

PlatformSupport.description: One operating system and the architectures a package supports on it.

PluginCapability.description: One capability a package may request. The vocabulary is closed.

PluginId.description: A plugin identifier from its manifest.

actions.description: The actions a control may invoke.

attachments.description: How the package contributes attachments, where it does.

capabilities.description: What the package asks to be permitted.

native_bridge.description: The native bridge recipe, where the package installs one.

payloads.description: Every byte the package consists of.

plugin_name.description: The plugin name under that publisher. Immutable for the package's life.

publisher_id.description: The publisher. Immutable for the package's life.

sdk_range.description: The SDK versions this package is written against.

wit_range.description:
The WIT package versions this package's component targets.

A package with no component still names the range it was authored against, because the
manifest shape it uses comes from the same release.

PluginName.description: A package-local plugin identifier, unique under its publisher.

Predicate.description: One term of a visibility predicate.

oneOf.description: Always visible.
Never visible.
True when the inner predicate is false.
True when every term is true.
True when at least one term is true.
True when the named capability is in the named state.

state.description: The state it must be in.

oneOf.description:
True when the actor currently holds the named right.

This hides a control the actor could not use. It never grants anything: the host checks
the right again at dispatch, and a predicate that lies only makes a control appear that
then fails the check.
True when the binding is in the named state.
True when the named node is present in the current document.
True when the named presentation fact holds.

PresentationFlag.description: A fact about the current presentation that a control can depend on.

oneOf.description: A pending approval resource exists in the ledger.
The upstream draft has text in it.
The client is a small screen.
The session has an attachment upload in progress.
The person holds the input lease.

PresentationManifest.description: The presentation manifest of one package.

base_revision.description:
The revision this document as a whole is at.

A delta names this revision as its base, so a client knows whether it can apply the delta
or must ask for a fresh snapshot.

nodes.description: The document nodes, in presentation order.

voice.description: The bounded projection a voice client receives.

ProgressState.description: How far along a progress node is.

oneOf.description: A known fraction of a known total.
Work is happening and its extent is unknown.
Work finished.
Work failed.

ProtocolPin.description:
The upstream protocol a table is pinned to.

A table is qualified against one installed protocol version. It is not carried forward to a
version nobody tested, because the classification of a method is exactly the kind of thing a
protocol revision changes.

name.description: The protocol name as the vendor publishes it.

qualified_range.description: The versions this table was qualified against.

tested_version.description: The exact version the publisher tested.

PublisherId.description: The publisher that signs and maintains a package. Immutable for the package's life.

PublisherRecord.description:
A publisher record.

Publishers are named in the index so a person can see who signed a package before installing
it, and so a delegation can be scoped to one publisher's path.

first_party.description: Whether this publisher ships with KalaReach.

homepage.description: Where the publisher's own source and contact details live.

findings.description: The findings, in the order they were produced.

RepositoryBudgets.description: The budgets a host sets when it enrols a repository.

full_offline_mirror.description: Whether every referenced payload is fetched rather than only what is installed.

RepositoryGeneration.description: The catalogue generation a plugin package was resolved against.

ResponseCorrelation.description: How a response is matched to its request.

oneOf.description: The response repeats the request identifier at a known path.

id_path.description: Where the identifier is in a response.

oneOf.description:
Responses arrive in request order on a single ordered channel.

The broker still records each opaque request before forwarding it, so ordering is how a
reply is matched, not a reason to skip the ledger.

RevocationReason.description: Why a package stops receiving new bindings.

oneOf.description: The publisher withdrew this release.
The release has a security defect.
The signing key was compromised.
A later release supersedes it and this one should not be installed again.

RevocationRecord.description:
A revocation record.

A revoked package stops new bindings. An active binding receives a warning and follows the
administrator's explicit disable policy; it does not change under a live request.

statement.description: What a person reads about it.

Route.description: One route from a native method to the stream that carries it.

method.description: The method as the table names it.

wire_name.description: The method name exactly as it appears on the wire.

RouteDirection.description: Which way a native method travels.

oneOf.description: The application asks KalaReach.
KalaReach asks the application.
Either side may send it.

SemanticPriority.description:
How prominently a client presents a control.

Priority is semantic, not visual: it says how important the action is, and each client decides
what that looks like on its own platform.

oneOf.description: The action a person came here to take.
A common alternative.
Rarely needed; a client may place it behind a menu.
Destructive or irreversible; a client presents it as such.

SourcePin.description:
The publisher's own record of where a package came from.

A reviewed catalogue entry pins the publisher, the source revision and the released package
digest. Runtime hosts install that release; they never execute a vendor repository's current
branch.

revision.description: The exact revision the package was built from.

StandardIcon.description: An icon from the standard set every client ships.

SubjectIdentity.description:
The exact identity the evidence was gathered against.

An installed upgrade does not invalidate an old running process's correctly pinned identity,
which is only expressible if the record names the identity rather than the product.

binary_digest.description: The digest of the tested binary, where the subject is a binary.

package_digest.description: The digest of that package's manifest.

plugin_id.description: The package the evidence is about, where it is about one.

publisher_id.description: The publisher whose signed record supplied the evidence, where one did.

schema_version.description: The version of the tested schema or protocol, where the subject is one.

Summary.description: The package summary. One line, no control or bidirectional characters.

TimestampMs.description: A UTC timestamp in milliseconds, as a decimal string in JSON.

ToolOutcome.description: The outcome of a tool call.

oneOf.description: Running.
Finished successfully.
Finished with an error.
Cancelled before it finished.

U64.description: An unsigned 64-bit counter. On the wire it is a CBOR unsigned integer; in JSON it is a decimal string.

UnsupportedNode.description:
A node whose kind this build does not know.

A client renders it as an unsupported-content block. It carries no body and therefore no
action: a newer package cannot reach a hidden action through a node an older client cannot
read.

kind.description: The kind the document claimed, for the unsupported-content block to name.

revision.description: The revision of the node that could not be read.

VersionRange.description: A semantic version range, such as '>=0.1, <0.2'. An unbounded range is rejected.

VoiceProjection.description:
What a voice client receives.

Voice gets status, pending choices and references to detail, never the whole document. A
spoken interface that reads an arbitrary document out loud is both unusable and a disclosure
nobody asked for.

choice_controls.description: The controls voice offers as choices.

detail_nodes.description: The nodes voice refers to without reading out.

status_nodes.description: The nodes whose status voice announces.

description: Generated from the Rust types in crates/kr-plugin-sdk. Rust is canonical: edit the Rust types and regenerate. Every property below names one root document; $defs holds the referenced types.

vocabulary.description: Every closed vocabulary in the package contract. This is a vocabulary rather than a document: it exists so each enumeration has one named type.
